title: Canada Holds New Student Arrivals at 150,000 a Year Through 2029
excerpt: Ottawa's 2027–2029 Immigration Levels Plan locks in the reduced student intake for three more years — up to 150,000 new arrivals a year inside a 370,000 temporary-resident ceiling, with no country quotas.
body:
• Canada's 2027–2029 Immigration Levels Plan holds new international student arrivals at up to 150,000 a year in each of 2027, 2028 and 2029.
  • The student figure sits inside a ceiling of 370,000 new temporary resident arrivals a year — 220,000 workers and up to 150,000 students — while permanent resident admissions stay at 380,000 a year.
  • The student target steps down from 155,000 for 2026 and is roughly half the 305,900 target set for 2025, according to published breakdowns of the plan.
  • For Indian applicants, there is no country quota: the 150,000 places form a single global pool, and the count covers new arrivals only — not study permit extensions or post-graduation work permits.

Canada will keep new international student arrivals capped at up to 150,000 a year through 2029, under the 2027–2029 Immigration Levels Plan released by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) on November 5 alongside the federal budget. The plan extends the reduced intake level already set for 2027 and 2028 by a further year, confirming that the tighter student regime introduced in 2024 is now the settled setting for the rest of the decade rather than a temporary squeeze.

"Permanent resident admissions are held at 380,000 a year, with the economic class maintained at 64.4% of admissions."

Who this affects

The target applies to new international students arriving in Canada under the International Student Programme — including the large number of applicants from India who apply for study permits each year. It does not count students already in Canada: study permit extensions, in-Canada applications and post-graduation work permits sit outside the arrivals figure, according to IRCC's supplementary information for the plan. The plan sets no quota by country, so Indian applicants compete for the same 150,000 places as applicants from everywhere else.

The numbers in the plan

IRCC's backgrounder states that targets for new temporary resident arrivals will stabilize at 370,000 per year for each of the next three years, comprising 220,000 new workers and up to 150,000 new international students in 2027, 2028 and 2029. The worker target splits into 170,000 arrivals under the International Mobility Program and 50,000 under the Temporary Foreign Worker Program. The overall temporary resident range is 355,000 to 385,000 a year.

Permanent resident admissions are held at 380,000 a year, with the economic class maintained at 64.4% of admissions. Family class admissions account for 21.3% — including 66,000 spouses, partners and children and 15,000 parents and grandparents a year. Francophone admissions outside Quebec are targeted to rise from 9.5% of admissions in 2027 to 12% in 2029. The full tables are in IRCC's supplementary information for the 2027–2029 plan.

How the student number got here

The 150,000 figure is the end of a steep climb-down. Canada introduced a cap on study permits in January 2024 after applications more than doubled between 2019 and 2023, and published breakdowns of the new plan put the student arrivals target at 305,900 for 2025 and 155,000 for 2026 before it settles at 150,000. IRCC says the targets support the government's commitment to reduce the temporary resident population and keep permanent resident admissions below 1% of Canada's population beyond 2027, allowing housing and services to catch up. The 2028 and 2029 figures are notional and are confirmed or adjusted by November 1 of the preceding year, so the out-years can still move.

What it means if you are applying from India

Nothing in the plan makes a study permit easier to obtain in 2027. Most applicants still need a provincial attestation letter from the province where they plan to study before IRCC will process the application, and the fixed global pool means competition for places stays intense even as the headline number stops falling. Students already in Canada are not part of the arrivals count, so those extending a permit or moving to a post-graduation work permit are not competing for these 150,000 places. Families weighing Canada against other destinations should plan on the capped regime lasting through 2029 — and should also weigh the permanent residence side of the plan, where 380,000 admissions a year and an increased Provincial Nominee Program allocation of 95,000 a year keep the study-to-PR pathway open, if narrower at the entry end. Our breakdown of the extra permanent residence spaces for 2027 and the latest IRCC processing times from India cover the other half of the picture.

The in-Canada measure

Alongside the levels plan, IRCC is introducing a time-limited measure to transition up to 200,000 people already living in Canada to permanent residence in 2027: a workers cohort of up to 100,000, transitioned with provinces and territories through increased Provincial Nominee Program allocations, and a humanitarian cohort of up to 100,000 people who have been waiting on decisions for years. IRCC says the measure will also help clear the remaining applications under the Hong Kong permanent residence pathways and the Ukraine Family Reunification Pathway.

What to do next

Prospective students should read the plan itself before relying on summaries: start with IRCC's backgrounder on the 2027–2029 Immigration Levels Plan, then check the study permit requirements and provincial attestation process on Canada.ca before applying. The next confirmation point is November 1, 2027, when the 2028 targets are confirmed or adjusted.
